newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - Asahi Bank reported New York problem - MOF.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Asahi Bank reported New York problem - MOF.

text.p: Officials of Asahi Bank Ltd have told Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) that they opened a U.S. Federal Reserve report that Japan's Kyodo news agency said was confidential, a senior MOF official told Reuters on Thursday.
Asked about the report on Kyodo earlier on Thursday, Sei Nakai, deputy director-general at MOF's Banking Bureau, said:
"We have been told about it by Asahi Bank. We will consider what course of action to take after U.S. authorities complete their investigations."
He said, however, that he could not understand why such a report would be left at a commercial bank.

Asahi Bank president Shigehiko Yoshino acknowledged earlier in the day in an interview with Kyodo that bank employees opened a sealed Federal Reserve inspection report on Asahi and said he realised the bank might face penalties.
"The act violates the Fed's internal rules and I suppose we will face some form of penalty," Yoshino said.
Yoshino said, however, that Asahi Bank had not incurred any huge losses at its New York branch, Kyodo reported.
"There is absolutely no case where we incurred large losses," Yoshino said in response to rumours that Asahi Bank's New York branch had incurred huge losses.
